title: Cursor as a Planner
shortDescription: Cursor helps break down complex tasks into manageable steps, creating structured plans before implementation.
detailedExplanation: Cursor analyzes your request and decomposes it into logical, sequential steps
It identifies dependencies between tasks and suggests an optimal order of execution
The planning phase helps catch potential issues before coding begins
Plans can be reviewed and refined through conversation before implementation
This mental model emphasizes thinking before doing, reducing wasted effort

title: Cursor as a Pair Programmer
shortDescription: Cursor acts as a collaborative coding partner, discussing approaches, reviewing code, and suggesting improvements in real-time.
detailedExplanation: Cursor engages in back-and-forth dialogue about code design and implementation choices
It provides context-aware suggestions based on your codebase and coding style
Like a human pair programmer, it asks clarifying questions when requirements are ambiguous
It can explain its reasoning and adapt to your feedback during the conversation
This collaborative approach leads to better solutions than one-way code generation

title: Cursor as a Code Reviewer
shortDescription: Cursor examines code for bugs, style issues, security vulnerabilities, and opportunities for improvement.
detailedExplanation: Cursor reviews code with a focus on correctness, maintainability, and best practices
It identifies potential bugs, edge cases, and security concerns before they reach production
The review process considers code style, naming conventions, and architectural patterns
It provides constructive feedback with explanations, not just error messages
This mental model helps maintain code quality and catch issues early in development

title: Cursor as a CI Fixer
shortDescription: Cursor automatically diagnoses and fixes CI/CD pipeline failures, test errors, and build issues.
detailedExplanation: When CI fails, Cursor analyzes error messages, logs, and test outputs to identify root causes
It suggests specific fixes for broken tests, compilation errors, and configuration issues
Cursor understands the relationship between code changes and CI failures
It can fix multiple related issues in a single pass, not just one error at a time
This mental model treats CI as a feedback loop that Cursor helps resolve efficiently

title: Cursor as a Knowledge Retriever
shortDescription: Cursor searches through your codebase, documentation, and context to find relevant information and answer questions.
detailedExplanation: Cursor indexes and understands your entire codebase, making information retrieval fast and accurate
It can answer questions about how code works, where features are implemented, and what patterns are used
The retrieval process considers context, not just keyword matching
It synthesizes information from multiple files and sources to provide comprehensive answers
This mental model positions Cursor as a searchable knowledge base of your project

title: Cursor as a Teacher
shortDescription: Cursor explains code concepts, teaches best practices, and helps developers understand how things work and why they matter.
detailedExplanation: Cursor breaks down complex code into understandable concepts, explaining not just what code does but why it's written that way
It teaches programming patterns, design principles, and best practices through contextual explanations
When you ask 'how does this work?' or 'why is this better?', Cursor provides educational answers that deepen understanding
It adapts explanations to your skill level, providing beginner-friendly introductions or advanced deep-dives as needed
This mental model positions Cursor as a patient tutor that helps you grow as a developer through continuous learning
